_about: Allowlist of meme formats a deck may use. Edit freely: ids are memegen.link template ids (https://api.memegen.link/templates), lines is how many captions the format takes, use tells the model when the format fits. Cartoon and animal formats only, on purpose: no real people's faces on a teacher's slide.

formats.name: Fancy Pooh
formats.use: a plain way vs a smarter way (top: weak habit, bottom: better habit)

formats.name: Spider-Man pointing
formats.use: two things that are really the same, or two sides pointing at each other

formats.name: This is fine
formats.use: calmly ignoring a problem that is clearly growing (top: setup, bottom: the calm line)

formats.name: X everywhere
formats.use: an idea that shows up everywhere (top: X, bottom: X everywhere)

formats.name: Philosoraptor
formats.use: a thought-provoking question that makes students stop and think

formats.name: Mocking SpongeBob
formats.use: mocking a common wrong claim (top: the claim, bottom: same claim in mocking case)

formats.name: Gru's plan
formats.use: a plan whose last step reveals a flaw (steps 1-2 sensible, 3-4 the same surprising result)

formats.name: Scooby-Doo reveal
formats.use: unmasking: what looks like X is really Y (villain, prompt, unmasked, reaction)

formats.name: Is this a pigeon?
formats.use: misidentifying a concept (person, the thing, 'Is this X?')

formats.name: Exit ramp
formats.use: swerving to the tempting option (option A, option B, the one chosen)

formats.name: Two buttons
formats.use: a hard choice between two options (option 1, option 2, the struggling person)

formats.name: X all the Y
formats.use: an over-enthusiastic rule (top: X, bottom: all the Y)

formats.name: Doge
formats.use: an excited, simple reaction to a satisfying idea

formats.name: Grumpy cat
formats.use: an unimpressed reaction to a common mistake
